cases.title: Exponential product: long proof

origin.upstream: V1 Chapter 14 section 14.2, R7 active source

obligations: D and evaluation v correctly typed
arbitrary source X and test f
construct both transposes and pair them
uniqueness first by transpose then product property
isomorphism via previously proved comparison theorem
reverse arrow and both inverse equations
cases.context:
Work in a category with the indicated products and supplied exponentials. For arrows $r:X\to B$ and $s:X\to C$, the product property gives a unique arrow $\langle r,s\rangle:X\to B\times C$ whose two projection composites are $r,s$. Thus two arrows into a product are equal when their corresponding projection composites are equal. For each supplied $B^A$, evaluation is $\ev_{B,A}:B^A\times A\to B$; for each $f:X\times A\to B$ there is a unique transpose $\Lambda f:X\to B^A$ with $\ev\circ(\Lambda f\times\id_A)=f$. The notation $\ev(g,h)$ abbreviates $\ev\circ\langle g,h\rangle$ for arrows with a common source. Exponential comparison means the following previously proved theorem: two objects with evaluations satisfying the same exponential property have a unique evaluation-compatible isomorphism, obtained by transposing each evaluation; both composites are identities by transpose uniqueness. For $b:B\to C$, $b^A$ denotes the transpose of $b\circ\ev_{B,A}$. A map $m:Y\to Z$ is monic if, for every object $W$ and all $g,h:W\to Y$, $m\circ g=m\circ h$ implies $g=h$. Composition is read right to left.
 The reader knows the implication symbol and equality of arrows into a product.

edits.after:

 p_Cv(u\times\id_A)=p_Cf.
\]
